summary.text: 妈 means “mother” or “mama.” It is the simplified form of 媽, built with 女 for a female-related meaning and 馬, a sound component whose older pronunciation was similar to that of 媽.

formation.text: The traditional graph 媽 is phonosemantic: 女 contributes a female-related meaning, and 馬 supplies a sound cue. In Zhengzhang Shangfang Old Chinese, 馬 *mraːʔ and 媽 *maːʔ share an initial and have broadly similar rhymes, though their vowels differ. 妈 retains 女 and uses simplified 马 for 馬.

components.text: 女 is the visible left component in 妈 and contributes the female-related meaning in this phono-semantic graph.
马 is the visible right component in 妈 and the simplified form of 馬, the phonetic component.

sound.text: In Zhengzhang Shangfang Old Chinese, 馬 *mraːʔ and 媽 *maːʔ share an initial and have broadly similar rhymes, though their vowels differ; this supports a probable phonetic relation.
In modern Standard Mandarin, 馬 mǎ and 媽 mā share an initial but differ in tone. This present-day resemblance does not establish their historical sound relationship.

history.text: 媽 is not recorded in Shuowen. The cited evidence gives no established earlier paleographic form or ancient graphic sequence; its visible sides are 女 and 馬.
In the standardized simplified graph 妈, 馬 is written as 马.

uncertainties.text: The proposed sound relation is supported here by a Zhengzhang Old Chinese comparison. No matched comparison from another reconstruction system is provided, and modern Mandarin readings alone do not establish the historical relationship.

senses.text: 妈 means ‘mother’ or ‘mama’ in present-day Chinese. The earliest attestation of this meaning is unresolved.

senses.gloss: form of address for female elders, older women, and servants in northern usage
senses.text: The character is also used to address female elders of the mother’s generation, older women, and, in northern usage, servants. The dates of these uses and their relationship to “mother” are unresolved.
An obsolete, isolated “mare; female horse” gloss is reported, but this does not establish a dated occurrence.

limitations.text: The dates and semantic links among the mother and female-address uses are unresolved. The reported obsolete “mare; female horse” gloss has no verified dated occurrence, and its relationship to the mother use is unknown.
A secondary account relates 媽 to 母 and proposes an older-language source, but the word history and any semantic path are not established here.

relationships.text: 女 contributes female-related meaning in 妈.

馬, written 马 in simplified 妈, is analyzed as the phonetic component. In Zhengzhang Old Chinese, 馬 *mraːʔ and 媽 *maːʔ share an initial and have broadly similar rhymes despite a vowel difference. Modern Mandarin mā and mǎ are a separate comparison and do not prove the historical relationship.
妈 is the standardized simplified counterpart of 媽; 馬 is written 马 in the simplified graph.
妈 means ‘mother’ or ‘mama’ in present-day Chinese. The earliest attestation of this meaning is unresolved.

The character is also used to address female elders of the mother’s generation, older women, and, in northern usage, servants. The dates of these uses and their relationship to “mother” are unresolved.
An obsolete, isolated “mare; female horse” gloss is reported, but this does not establish a dated occurrence.

overview.text: 妈 means ‘mother’ or ‘mama.’ 女 contributes female-related meaning, while 马 is the simplified form of 馬, the probable sound component.

components.text: 女 contributes female-related meaning in 妈.
马 is the simplified form of 馬, the sound component. In the cited older pronunciations, they share an initial and have broadly similar rhymes, though their vowels differ.

limitations.text: No historical glyph image could be confirmed as a usable, rights-cleared image of 媽. The cited 龍龕手鑑 image link failed, and the other image leads did not establish a usable candidate. No early graphic form is established by the available evidence.

evidence.text: The entry analyzes 媽 as semantic 女 plus phonetic 馬 and lists Zhengzhang Shangfang Old Chinese 馬 *mraːʔ and 媽 *maːʔ. Within that named system, the forms share an initial and have a broad rhyme resemblance, with a vowel difference. This is a secondary source’s phonetic-series analysis, not evidence for an ancient graphic sequence or a dated sense history.
evidence.title: 媽 — Wiktionary

evidence.source: National Taiwan Normal University, Mandarin Training Center, 漢字簡介: Writing Chinese Characters
evidence.text: The instructional text uses 媽 mā ‘mother’ as an example of a phono-semantic compound: 女 nǚ indicates meaning and 馬 mǎ is the phonetic. This independently supports the conventional component-role analysis, though it is a teaching overview rather than a paleographic study.
evidence.title: 漢字簡介 — Writing Chinese Characters

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Revised Mandarin Chinese Dictionary
evidence.text: The entry records 媽 as a term of address for one’s mother, female elders of the mother’s generation, servants in northern usage, and older women. The dictionary does not date these uses or establish a semantic sequence among them.

evidence.field: 妈 entry; 字形结构 / 字形分析 / 基本解释 / 详细解释
evidence.text: The entry for 妈 (U+5988) identifies it as a left-right graph analyzed as 形声；从女、马声. It lists mother and female-elder address senses without marking them obsolete, supporting current use. This directly supports a current-form decomposition and the 女 semantic and 马 phonetic analysis; it does not establish ancient graphic history.

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: A00958 媽; 字樣說明; 釋義
evidence.text: The entry specifies current 媽 as left 女 and right 馬, notes that it is not recorded in Shuowen, and cites 龍龕手鑑．女部：「媽，母也」. It also lists address senses for a mother, female elders of the mother's generation, servants in northern usage, and older women. This corroborates the traditional graph’s present components and the dictionary-cited mother gloss, but does not itself date those senses or establish their development sequence.

Under the 怕 headword, the passage says its colloquial reading history is analogous to using 爸妈 instead of 父母: initials and finals changed over time in speech while older readings continued in the literary register. This is a pronunciation analogy only; it gives no etymology, historical reading, or component analysis for 妈. No OCR correction is proposed.

context.provenance: Base evidence consists of imported local JSONL excerpts. Source names identify upstream datasets; extraction may lose sense and language boundaries. Further external evidence and research activity are documented separately in the dossier.
editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

search_audit.query: Repository 字源 corpus occurrences of 妈/媽 and the supplied PDF p. 951 candidate
search_audit.outcome: Searched the local provisional OCR corpus. Candidate PDF p. 951 is a 怕 entry whose paragraph contains 爸妈 only as a spoken-reading analogy; no 妈/媽 headword or etymology occurs there. I inspected the source scan pixels for that page. The corpus also contains index/reference mentions, which are not a headed 媽 entry.

gaps: The local repository rows requested for Unihan and Baxter–Sagart could not be checked in this browser-only research stage. In particular, the cited Wiktionary entry gives Baxter Middle Chinese muX, while dossier metadata gives Guangyun 明一模上 / fanqie 莫補; these are compatible descriptive records but not independently cross-checked against the local Baxter–Sagart file.

Official Unicode GetUnihanData pages for U+5ABD and U+5988 were attempted and inaccessible. Therefore exact current kMandarin rows were not verified or cited as successful evidence. A Unicode search interface was inspected only for what its kMandarin field means.

No inspected primary paleographic witness demonstrates an early form of 媽. The MOE reference explicitly says it is not in Shuowen; its shape table lists several paleographic resources as unavailable. No claim about oracle-bone, bronze, seal, clerical, or corruption stages is established here.

The MOE dictionary cites the 龍龕手鑑 gloss but the character-level image was not inspected. The dictionary is a Liao-period work dated 997 in secondary metadata found during search, but no primary page was opened to verify the date or exact witness. Thus the earliest dated attestation of the mother sense remains not independently verified from the primary source.

The entry's colloquial relation of 媽 to 母 and any proposed Proto-Sino-Tibetan source are secondary etymological claims. This research did not independently establish the spoken-word genealogy or the semantic path from an older female/woman term to ‘mother’; graphic history and word history remain distinct.

Wiktionary lists an obsolete ‘mare’ sense without an inspected dated citation. Its date, relation to the mother sense, and whether this is an unrelated use remain unresolved; do not infer chronology from the list of glosses.

The phonetic analysis has system-specific support in Zhengzhang reconstructions, but no independent reconstruction-system comparison or local Baxter–Sagart row comparison was completed. Current Mandarin mā alone cannot establish the ancient sound relation.

No usable direct image URL with verified image identity and reuse rights was established. MOE's candidate image link failed; Commons and Xiaoxuetang searches did not produce a verified suitable image. Therefore no glyph candidates are proposed.

No primary paleographic witness for 媽 was visually inspected. The MOE entry states the character is absent from Shuowen and lists major oracle-bone, bronze, seal and other shape references as unavailable. No ancient formation stage or graphic corruption is established.

The 龍龕手鑑 mother gloss is cited by the MOE dictionary, but the target primary page image was not inspected. The opened volume page establishes attribution to Liao monk 行均 but does not display the 女部 passage. Earliest dated attestation is therefore not independently verified at primary-page level.

The proposed 女 semantic plus 馬 phonetic account is supported by dossier secondary excerpts and standard component analysis; no new source page with an independently inspectable sound-series argument was verified here. The source word for the 馬 graph is the word ‘horse’, but a sound-component claim does not depend on reconstructing an original depicted horse name. Local Baxter–Sagart data gives 馬 *mˤraʔ but contains no 媽 row, preventing same-system comparison.

The local Unihan rows establish current mā for 媽/妈 and mǎ for 馬. Character-specific Unicode records were inaccessible, so the required official click-through references could not be verified. The external Unihan search interface documents the property only generally.

Later uses for female elders, servants and older women are listed by the MOE dictionary, but their dates and semantic links to the mother address sense remain undated here. The reported ‘mare’ gloss in dossier Wiktionary evidence has no verified dated citation; its relationship to the mother sense remains unresolved.

The local source Baxter–Sagart row uses *mˤraʔ for 馬; dossier Wiktionary provides Zhengzhang's *mraːʔ for 馬 and *maːʔ for 媽. These are different reconstruction systems and must not be merged. Exact Zhengzhang host/component phonetic comparison was not independently rechecked during this run.

[SCAN VERIFICATION REQUIRED] 字源 2012, PDF p. 1102 (printed p. 1087), running header contains 妈/媽 among unrelated entries, but the page’s article text covers other headwords; do not cite it as a 媽 entry. The source corpus also has index and pronunciation-index mentions, not a verified standalone 媽 headword. A targeted search found no headed entry for 媽/妈 in the inspected relevant corpus hits.

The 字源 2012 passage on PDF p. 951 (printed p. 936) was directly inspected for its exact 怕 headword and paragraph; its scan supports only the spoken-pronunciation analogy involving 爸妈. No book evidence here establishes 媽’s ancient graph, the 女/M馬 component roles, or earliest use.

The MOE dictionary cites the 龍龕手鑑 mother gloss and gives its location as volume 2, 女部, p. 39 right, but that primary page image was not inspected. The earliest dated attestation and exact primary witness therefore remain unverified.

No primary paleographic form or graphic change for 媽 was established. The MOE entry says it is not recorded in Shuowen and marks several early-script reference categories unavailable; that does not prove absence from all early corpora.

No matched Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese reading for 媽 was verified. The local dossier row reports 馬 *mˤraʔ, while Wiktionary reports Zhengzhang 馬 *mraːʔ and 媽 *maːʔ; these are distinct systems and should not be merged. Current Mandarin resemblance alone does not establish the historical sound relation.

The character-specific Unicode Unihan pages for 妈, 媽 and 馬 were inaccessible. Local readings supplied in the input show 妈 mā and 馬 mǎ, but the required external official per-character click-through verification was not obtained.

The MOE and Revised Mandarin dictionaries list broader address uses, but their dates and links to the mother sense are not established here. Wiktionary’s obsolete ‘mare’ gloss was not independently dated or linked to the mother sense.

The visible 女 and 馬 sides of current 媽 are directly confirmed by the MOE entry, and current 妈 is directly analyzed as 女 plus 马 by 汉典. These sources do not establish a paleographic sequence or ancient graphic origin; MOE reports 媽 absent from Shuowen and marks several early-script reference categories unavailable.
字源, PDF p. 951 (printed p. 936), supports only the 爸妈/父母 pronunciation analogy in the 怕 entry. It does not support claims about 妈’s formation, sound history, or earliest attestation.

limitations.text: No historical glyph image could be confirmed as a usable, rights-cleared image of 媽. The cited 龍龕手鑑 image link failed, and the other image leads did not establish a usable candidate. No early graphic form is established by the available evidence.
